title: the four weddings
hook: one wedding becomes four, and two families tell their whole histories first

segments.voice: Yesterday: Janaka's bow, part three. Rama asked first, lifted it as if in play, and the bow broke like thunder. Did you ask before picking up something that wasn't yours? Day five hundred ten.

Janaka's messengers ride hard to Ayodhya. They stand before Dasharatha, the king who just weeks ago begged a sage not to take his teenage son, and they tell him: your Rama broke Shiva's bow. Your Lakshmana is with him, safe. King Janaka asks you to come to Mithila for the wedding. You can imagine the old man's face. The next morning, Dasharatha sets out with Vasishtha, his priests, his army and his treasure, and travels to Mithila. When the two kings meet, they embrace like family before they are family.
screen: `MESSENGERS RIDE TO AYODHYA.` → `YOUR RAMA BROKE SHIVA'S BOW.` → `TWO KINGS EMBRACE.`

segments.voice: Before anyone marries, the families do something we might find surprising. They recite their family trees, aloud, all the way back. Vasishtha stands and names the line of Ikshvaku, generation after generation: from Brahma, through Manu, Ikshvaku himself, kings like Sagara, whose sons dug the ocean, and Bhagiratha, who brought the Ganga down from heaven, all the way to Dasharatha. Then Janaka names his own line from King Nimi down, including Devarata, who received the bow. Why? Because in this world a wedding isn't two people meeting. It's two long stories joining. Then Janaka makes the formal gift. Sita to Rama. And his second daughter, Urmila, to Lakshmana. And then a lovely thing happens. Vishvamitra and Vasishtha together suggest something more. Janaka's younger brother, Kushadhvaja, has two daughters too, Mandavi and Shrutakirti. Why not give them to Bharata and Shatrughna? Janaka agrees with joy. So one wedding becomes four. Four brothers, four sisters and cousins, two royal houses woven together in a single day. Before the ceremony, Dasharatha gives away an enormous gift of cows in his sons' names, and a final guest arrives: Yudhajit, Bharata's uncle from Kaikeyi's family. Nothing that's about to happen in this family will be private. Every joy, and every grief to come, will belong to all of them.
screen: `THE FAMILY TREES, ALOUD.` · `SITA TO RAMA, URMILA TO LAKSHMANA.` · `MANDAVI AND SHRUTAKIRTI, TOO.` · `ONE WEDDING BECOMES FOUR.` · then, large: `TWO HOUSES, ONE DAY.`

segments.voice: Sit and settle. Bring to mind the people who came before you: parents or the ones who raised you, grandparents, names you know, names you don't. You don't need to know them all. Just feel the line of them, stretching back, ending here, in this breath. If you pray, you can remember them in your own way. Breathe in, and feel them behind you. The bell holds the time.
The four weddings. Rama and Sita, Lakshmana and Urmila, Bharata and Mandavi, Shatrughna and Shrutakirti: two royal houses joined in one day.
Your line: the four weddings. Today, ask an older relative or friend one question about their parents or grandparents, and listen to the answer. Day five hundred ten.

screen: `DAY 510 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: THE FOUR WEDDINGS, PART TWO.`

howItsDone: In many Hindu weddings, priests still recite the gotra and lineage of the bride's and groom's families before the ceremony, a custom echoed in Vasishtha's and Janaka's recitations in the Ramayana.

myth: all four brothers marry, to Janaka's daughters and his brother Kushadhvaja's.

fork.setup: you're Janaka. two sages suggest your brother's daughters marry Bharata and Shatrughna. what do you say?
options: only if Dasharatha pays a bride-price.
fork.reveal: he agrees gladly, and one wedding becomes four, joining the two houses.

original.note: Sanskrit vivāha: marriage, the wedding rite; from a root meaning to carry or lead away.

trapdoor: what you thought: the Ramayana has one royal wedding.
what it means: it has four, and they bind two whole families before any trouble begins.
what a scholar hears: Bala Kanda 70–72 give both lineages in full, from Brahma to Dasharatha and from Nimi to Janaka; Urmila is Janaka's daughter, Mandavi and Shrutakirti Kushadhvaja's.

sources.ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Bala Kanda 68–69 (messengers to Ayodhya; Dasharatha travels to Mithila)
Valmiki Ramayana, Bala Kanda 70–72 (the lineages; the four brides; Dasharatha's gifts)

notes: 'Just weeks ago' for the time since Vishvamitra's visit is approximate; the text doesn't give a duration.
Lineage names (Sagara, Bhagiratha, Nimi, Devarata) chosen as ones the script is confident appear in the recitations; confirm.
Yudhajit's arrival at Mithila before the weddings: confirm placement (sarga 73 in the vulgate).
Root of vivaha (vi + vah, to carry or lead): confirm.
